intent.raw_query: Cambodia Angkor Wat + beaches, $1100, 10 days, November 2026

selected_hotel.name: Angkor Archaeological Park, Siem Reap Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Angkor Wat Temple Complex Sunrise Tour
experiences.description: Explore the world's largest religious monument at sunrise, wandering through the iconic towers and intricate bas-reliefs of Angkor Wat, then continue to the mysterious Bayon temple with its 216 serene stone faces and the jungle-engulfed Ta Prohm temple made famous by Tomb Raider.

experiences.name: Phnom Penh Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda Visit
experiences.description: Tour the stunning Royal Palace complex and the adjacent Silver Pagoda, home to a life-sized gold Buddha encrusted with 9,584 diamonds. Gain deep insight into Khmer royal history, Buddhist traditions, and Cambodian cultural heritage through ornate architecture and sacred artifacts.

experiences.name: Koh Rong Samloem Beach Day
experiences.description: Spend a day on one of Southeast Asia's most pristine and unspoiled beaches, with crystal-clear turquoise waters, powdery white sand, and vibrant coral reefs. Snorkel among tropical fish, relax in hammocks strung between palm trees, and witness spectacular bioluminescent plankton after dark.

experiences.name: Khmer Cooking Class and Phsar Thmei Market Tour
experiences.description: Begin with a guided walk through the iconic Art Deco Central Market sampling local street food, then join a hands-on cooking class to master traditional Khmer dishes such as Fish Amok, Lok Lak, and Mango Salad. Learn about the unique blend of spices, herbs, and flavors that define Cambodian cuisine.

experiences.name: Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum and Killing Fields Tour
experiences.description: Visit the sobering S-21 prison turned museum at Tuol Sleng, then travel to the Choeung Ek Killing Fields memorial to understand the tragic history of the Khmer Rouge era through preserved artifacts, survivor testimonies, and a deeply moving audio guide. An essential and respectful journey through Cambodia's modern history.
experiences.location: Tuol Sleng and Choeung Ek, Phnom Penh

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Cambodia
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Angkor Archaeological Park, Siem Reap Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00. Rest and transit time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Siem Reap International Airport at 13:00. Clear immigration and customs, collect luggage, and take a budget tuk-tuk (~$5–7) to your boutique stay near Angkor Archaeological Park. Check in, freshen up, and take a slow walk around the immediate hotel surroundings to orient yourself. Visit the nearby Angkor National Museum entrance area to get a feel for the neighborhood (no entry needed today).
day_by_day.evening: Stroll to Pub Street and the Old Market (Phsar Chas) area in central Siem Reap — about 15–20 minutes by tuk-tuk. Browse the night market stalls, soak in the lively atmosphere, and pick up a cold Angkor Beer at a street-side bar.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a snack at the airport on arrival.
meals.lunch: Quick bite at the airport or a roadside stall near the hotel on arrival — try a $1–2 baguette sandwich (num pang), a French-Khmer legacy snack.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Khmer Kitchen Restaurant on The Alley near Pub Street — budget-friendly authentic Khmer dishes like amok fish curry and lok lak for $3–6 per dish.

day_by_day.notes: Purchase a 3-day Angkor Pass ($62 USD) tonight or first thing tomorrow morning at the Angkor ticket office — it is valid for any 3 days within a week. Carry USD cash as it is widely accepted. Tuk-tuks are the best budget transport option in Siem Reap.

day_by_day.morning: Rise before dawn (4:30 AM) and hire a tuk-tuk (~$15–18 for a full-day Angkor tour) to witness the iconic sunrise over Angkor Wat. Arrive by 5:15 AM to secure a spot at the reflecting pool. Spend the morning exploring Angkor Wat's galleries, bas-reliefs depicting the Churning of the Ocean of Milk, and its five central towers. This is the world's largest religious monument and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Angkor temple circuit with visits to Angkor Thom — enter through the South Gate with its 54 stone faces, explore the Bayon Temple (faces of Avalokiteshvara), the Baphuon, Phimeanakas, and the Terrace of the Elephants. End with a visit to Ta Prohm, the jungle-enveloped temple famously used in the Tomb Raider film, where massive strangler fig trees grow through ancient stone walls.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel to rest and shower. Head out for a relaxed dinner near Pub Street, then visit the Angkor Night Market for souvenir shopping — silk scarves, handmade crafts, and Khmer artwork at negotiable prices.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and banana pancake from a street vendor near the Angkor Wat entrance gate (~$1–2) before sunrise.
meals.lunch: Eat at one of the open-air local restaurants just outside the Angkor complex near Ta Prohm — a plate of fried rice or noodle soup costs $2–4.
meals.dinner: Try Chamkar Vegetarian Restaurant or Bugs Cafe (adventurous!) near Pub Street — meals from $4–8. Or grab a cheap bowl of kuy teav (rice noodle soup) from a street stall for $1.50.

day_by_day.notes: Start your Angkor Pass today (Day 1 of 3). Wear lightweight, breathable clothing and sturdy walking shoes. Bring a refillable water bottle — dehydration is common. Shoulders and knees must be covered to enter temples. November weather in Siem Reap is generally pleasant and dry, making it ideal temple-visiting weather.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early by tuk-tuk to explore the outer Angkor temples. Visit Banteay Srei, located about 25 km northeast of Siem Reap — known as the 'Citadel of Women,' it features extraordinarily intricate pink sandstone carvings and is considered one of the finest examples of Khmer art. The detail in the lintels, pediments, and devata figures is breathtaking.
day_by_day.afternoon: On the way back, stop at Banteay Samré, a well-preserved but less-visited temple surrounded by a moat. Then visit Pre Rup, a 10th-century state temple-mountain with great views from the top — a popular sunset spot. Spend the late afternoon exploring Neak Pean, an artificial island temple, and Ta Som, a small but beautiful jungle temple.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Apsara dance performance — Smile of Angkor or Apsara Theatre offer budget shows for $12–18 including dinner buffet, giving you both cultural entertainment and a meal in one.

meals.breakfast: Eat at your hotel or a nearby local café — try bai sach chrouk (grilled pork over rice) for $1.50–2.50, a classic Cambodian breakfast.
meals.lunch: Pack snacks from a local market or eat at a roadside stall near Banteay Srei — noodle dishes and fresh fruit available for $1–3.
meals.dinner: Included in the Apsara dinner-show package, or opt out of the show and eat at a local restaurant near the Old Market for $3–5.

day_by_day.notes: Day 2 of your 3-day Angkor Pass. Banteay Srei is farther out so negotiate a tuk-tuk day rate (~$20–25) that covers all stops. Bring sunscreen and a hat — the outer temples have less tree cover. Photography is excellent at Banteay Srei in morning light.

day_by_day.morning: Use your final Angkor Pass day to visit the lesser-known but spectacular temples. Head to Beng Mealea, a remote jungle temple about 40 km east of Siem Reap (~$15–20 tuk-tuk round trip). Often called 'the jungle temple,' it is largely unrestored, with massive stone blocks tumbled by centuries of vegetation — an adventurer's dream with far fewer tourists than Ta Prohm.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Siem Reap and visit Preah Khan, a sprawling temple complex dedicated to the father of King Jayavarman VII, featuring long corridors, libraries, and a unique two-story circular structure. Then explore East Mebon, built on an artificial island in the middle of the former Eastern Baray reservoir, featuring elephant statues at its corners.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the vibrant Phsar Leu (Upper Market) — a local market where residents shop, offering an authentic non-touristy experience. Pick up fresh tropical fruits, snacks, and local products at rock-bottom prices. End the evening with a traditional Khmer massage (~$6–8/hour) at one of many reputable budget massage parlors near Pub Street.

meals.breakfast: Eat at a local café near your hotel — try nom banh chok (Khmer noodles with green fish curry sauce), a traditional Cambodian breakfast for $1–2.
meals.lunch: Bring packed snacks to Beng Mealea or eat at the small restaurant on-site for $3–5.
meals.dinner: Street food dinner at the Siem Reap night market — grilled skewers, spring rolls, papaya salad, and fresh coconut for $3–5 total.

day_by_day.notes: Final day of your 3-day Angkor Pass — make it count! Beng Mealea has a $5 separate entry fee on top of your Angkor Pass. Start early to beat the midday heat. After today, you will have covered the major Angkor highlights comprehensively.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning trip to Tonlé Sap Lake — the largest freshwater lake in Southeast Asia and a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve. Book a budget boat tour (~$10–15) from the nearby Chong Kneas floating village. Observe the extraordinary floating communities where entire villages — homes, schools, churches, and pig farms — float on the lake's surface. The lake dramatically changes size between wet and dry seasons.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Kampong Khleang floating village (slightly farther but more authentic and less touristy than Chong Kneas) or take a tuk-tuk to the Artisans Angkor workshop in central Siem Reap — a free-entry silk and stone-carving workshop that trains disadvantaged Cambodian youth. Watch craftspeople at work and browse (no obligation to buy) beautiful handmade goods.
day_by_day.evening: Prepare for travel to Phnom Penh tomorrow. Take a relaxed evening walk through the Siem Reap River Walk (Riverside Road) — lined with cafés, bars, and restaurants. Enjoy a farewell drink in Siem Reap at Miss Wong cocktail bar (happy hour specials) or a cheap beer at a street-side plastic-stool bar.

meals.breakfast: Grab a fresh baguette with butter and condensed coffee (café sua da style) from a local bakery stall for $1–2.
meals.lunch: Eat fresh fish amok or grilled river fish at a local restaurant near the Tonlé Sap lake dock for $3–5.
meals.dinner: Budget dinner at Khmer BBQ (Malis or a local equivalent) — tabletop grills where you cook your own meats and vegetables for $5–8 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book your Siem Reap to Phnom Penh bus ticket today for tomorrow morning — Giant Ibis or Mekong Express buses are reliable and comfortable (~$9–13). The journey takes about 6 hours. Book online or at any guesthouse travel desk.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Siem Reap by 7:00–8:00 AM bus to Phnom Penh (Giant Ibis recommended, ~$13). The scenic 6-hour ride passes through rural Cambodian countryside, rice paddies, and small towns. Arrive in Phnom Penh around 13:00–14:00. Check into a budget guesthouse near the riverside (~$8–15/night for a clean dorm or private room — try Mad Monkey Hostel or Onederz Hostel).
day_by_day.afternoon: After settling in, visit the Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda complex ($10 entry). The palace features stunning Khmer and French colonial architecture. The Silver Pagoda — named for its floor of 5,000 silver tiles — houses priceless Buddhist artifacts including a life-size gold Buddha encrusted with 9,584 diamonds. Dress code: covered shoulders and knees required.
day_by_day.evening: Walk along the Phnom Penh Riverside Promenade (Sisowath Quay) as the sun sets over the Tonlé Sap and Mekong rivers confluence. Browse the riverside night market stalls and grab street food. Visit the lively FCC (Foreign Correspondents' Club) for a sunset drink with river views (one drink budget splurge, ~$4–6).

meals.breakfast: Eat before boarding the bus — grab a banh mi sandwich or rice porridge from a street vendor near the Siem Reap bus station for $1–2.
meals.lunch: The Giant Ibis bus includes a meal stop — eat at the rest stop restaurant for $2–4, or bring snacks from Siem Reap.
meals.dinner: Dinner at a local Phnom Penh restaurant near the riverside — try Romdeng (social enterprise restaurant serving traditional Khmer cuisine, slightly pricier at $6–10) or a riverside street stall for $2–4.

day_by_day.notes: Phnom Penh is Cambodia's capital and a bustling, complex city. Keep valuables secure and be aware of bag-snatching from motorbikes on busy streets. Tuk-tuks and PassApp (Cambodian ride-hailing app) are the best budget transport options in the city.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum (S-21) — a former high school converted into a brutal Khmer Rouge prison between 1975–1979 ($3 entry + optional audio guide $3). This deeply moving and historically significant site documents the atrocities committed during Pol Pot's regime. Over 17,000 people were imprisoned here; only seven survived. Allow 2–3 hours and approach with respect and sensitivity.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a tuk-tuk (~30 min) to the Choeung Ek Genocidal Center — the infamous 'Killing Fields' ($6 entry with audio guide). Walk the peaceful memorial grounds where mass graves were discovered, listen to survivor testimonies on the audio guide, and pay respects at the Buddhist stupa filled with the skulls and bones of victims. A profoundly important and sobering historical experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the city center and decompress with a walk through the Central Market (Phsar Thmei) — a stunning Art Deco yellow dome market built in 1937 selling jewelry, clothing, electronics, and local goods. Browse without pressure. End the evening with dinner and a stroll along the riverside, reflecting on the day's experiences.

meals.breakfast: Eat at a local café near your guesthouse — bai sach chrouk (grilled pork rice) or congee for $1.50–2.50.
meals.lunch: Eat near Tuol Sleng at a local restaurant — a bowl of pho or fried rice for $2–3.
meals.dinner: Try Friends Restaurant (Mith Samlanh) near the riverside — a social enterprise training vulnerable youth in hospitality. Excellent Cambodian tapas for $4–8 per dish.

day_by_day.notes: Today is emotionally heavy but historically essential. The Khmer Rouge period (1975–1979) resulted in the deaths of an estimated 1.5–2 million Cambodians — nearly 25% of the population. Take breaks as needed. The audio guide at Choeung Ek is highly recommended and included in the entry fee.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the National Museum of Cambodia ($10 entry) — an elegant terracotta building housing the world's finest collection of Khmer art, including pre-Angkorian bronze statues, stone sculptures, and royal artifacts spanning 1,000 years of Cambodian civilization. Spend 2 hours here for excellent historical context after your Angkor temple visits.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a tuk-tuk to Wat Phnom — a hilltop temple and the spiritual heart of Phnom Penh, founded in 1372 according to legend by a woman named Penh (giving the city its name). Then take an afternoon bus or shared taxi (~$10–13, 3–4 hours) toward Kampot, a charming riverside colonial town in southern Cambodia — your base for beach exploration.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Kampot by early evening. Check into a budget guesthouse (~$8–15/night — try Blissful Guesthouse or Mad Monkey Kampot). Take a slow walk along the Kampot River promenade, admire the French colonial architecture, and settle in with a cold drink at a riverside bar.

meals.breakfast: Eat at a Phnom Penh café — try a num pang sandwich with pâté and pickled vegetables for $1.50, a Cambodian-French fusion staple.
meals.lunch: Quick lunch near the National Museum — a local noodle shop for $2–3.
meals.dinner: Dinner in Kampot at Rikitikitavi or a riverside local restaurant — fresh Kampot pepper crab or prawn dishes for $5–8, or cheap local rice dishes for $2–3.

day_by_day.notes: Kampot is famous for its world-renowned Kampot pepper — considered among the finest pepper in the world. Try it on everything! The town has a relaxed, bohemian atmosphere very different from Siem Reap and Phnom Penh. Rent a bicycle (~$2–3/day) to explore the town at your own pace.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a bicycle or motorbike (~$5–8/day) and explore the Kampot countryside. Visit a Kampot pepper plantation — La Plantation or Sothy's Pepper Farm offer free or low-cost guided tours showing the entire pepper cultivation process. Taste the difference between red, black, and white Kampot pepper fresh from the vine — a unique agricultural and cultural experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Kep — a small beach town 25 km from Kampot (tuk-tuk ~$8–10 one way). Visit Kep's famous Crab Market, where you can buy freshly caught crabs directly from fishing boats and have them cooked on the spot with Kampot pepper sauce for $5–8 — one of Cambodia's most iconic and affordable culinary experiences. Swim at Kep Beach (small but pleasant) or take a short boat trip to Rabbit Island (Koh Tonsay) for $5 return — a pristine island with white sand, clear water, and basic beach bungalows.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Kampot for sunset. Take a sunset boat cruise on the Kampot River (~$5–8 per person on a shared boat) — watch the sun dip behind Bokor Mountain as fireflies begin to light up the mangroves. End the evening with dinner and drinks at a riverside bar.

meals.breakfast: Eat at a local Kampot café — try a fresh fruit smoothie bowl or French-style breakfast (baguette, butter, jam, coffee) for $2–3.
meals.lunch: Crab with Kampot pepper sauce at the Kep Crab Market — this IS the meal of the trip. Budget $6–10 for a whole crab cooked to order.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Epic Arts Café in Kampot (social enterprise supporting deaf and disabled Cambodians) or a riverside local restaurant — $4–7 for a full meal.

day_by_day.notes: November is a great time to visit Kep and Kampot — the rainy season has just ended, making the landscape lush and green with calm seas. Rabbit Island is highly recommended for a few hours of beach relaxation. Bring sunscreen and cash (limited ATMs in Kep).

day_by_day.morning: Rise early for a final morning in Kampot. Rent a bicycle and ride to Phnom Chhngok Cave Temple — a hidden gem 8 km from Kampot where a 7th-century Khmer brick temple sits inside a dramatic cave system ($1 entry + small tip for the local guide). Climb the hill for panoramic views over the Kampot River and countryside. A perfect blend of history, nature, and culture to close the trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Kampot, pack up, and take a shared taxi or bus back to Phnom Penh (~$10–13, 3–4 hours) for onward travel, or head directly to Sihanoukville for a final beach afternoon if your departure allows. If returning to Phnom Penh for a flight, use any remaining time to pick up last-minute souvenirs at the Russian Market (Phsar Toul Tom Poung) — the best place for quality, locally made souvenirs at fair prices.
day_by_day.evening: Final dinner in Phnom Penh or at the airport. Reflect on 10 incredible days spanning ancient temples, genocide history, floating villages, pepper plantations, and coastal beauty — a comprehensive journey through Cambodia's soul.

meals.breakfast: Final Cambodian breakfast at a local Kampot café — nom banh chok (Khmer noodles) or bai sach chrouk for $1.50–2.50.
meals.lunch: Eat at the bus rest stop or grab snacks for the road — $2–4.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a restaurant of your choice in Phnom Penh — splurge slightly on your last night at Malis Restaurant (upscale Khmer cuisine, $10–15) or keep it budget at a riverside street stall ($3–5).

day_by_day.notes: Budget summary for the 10-day trip: Angkor Pass $62, accommodation ~$80–120 (budget guesthouses), food ~$3–8/day = ~$30–80, transport ~$50–70, activities ~$30–40. Total estimated budget: $250–370 USD for 10 days, excluding international flights. Cambodia is one of Southeast Asia's most rewarding budget destinations — your dollar goes far and the cultural richness is unmatched.

trip_options.title: Classic Cambodia Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Angkor Archaeological Park, Siem Reap Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Siem Reap International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Rest and transit time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check into your Boutique Stay near Angkor Archaeological Park. Freshen up, then take a leisurely tuk-tuk ride to the nearby Angkor Wat outer grounds for a gentle first look at the temple silhouette without entering. Stroll the reflecting pool promenade and soak in the iconic views.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Pub Street area in Siem Reap town for a classic first-night Cambodian dinner. Explore the lively night market at Angkor Night Market for local handicrafts and souvenirs.

meals.breakfast: Meal on flight or grab a snack at the airport upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Light bite at a café near the hotel after check-in — try 'The Blue Pumpkin' for sandwiches and smoothies (~$5–8).
meals.dinner: Dinner at 'Mahob Restaurant' on Pub Street for authentic Khmer cuisine — amok fish curry, lok lak beef (~$12–18 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Exchange currency to Cambodian Riel (KHR) or keep USD — both are widely accepted. Purchase a 3-day Angkor Pass ($62) at the ticket office today if time permits, as it opens until 17:30. Tuk-tuk from airport to hotel ~$8–10.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn wake-up for the iconic Angkor Wat sunrise (arrive by 05:15). Watch the sun rise over the five towers reflected in the lotus pond — one of the world's most breathtaking spectacles. Spend the morning exploring the temple's bas-relief galleries, the Gallery of a Thousand Buddhas, and the central sanctuary.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Angkor Thom complex — the massive South Gate with its stone face towers, the Bayon Temple (famous for 216 serene stone faces), the Elephant Terrace, and the Terrace of the Leper King. Hire a knowledgeable local guide (~$25–35/half day) for rich historical context.
day_by_day.evening: Return to hotel for rest during the hottest part of late afternoon. Evening visit to Ta Prohm temple (the 'Tomb Raider' temple) at golden hour when crowds thin and light filters beautifully through the jungle canopy.

meals.breakfast: Early pre-sunrise coffee and pastries packed from the hotel or a nearby stall. Proper breakfast after sunrise at 'Vibe Café' near Angkor (~$4–7).
meals.lunch: Lunch at 'Angkor Café' near Angkor Wat — a mid-range option with air conditioning, Khmer and Western dishes (~$8–12).
meals.dinner: Dinner at 'Cuisine Wat Damnak' — a renowned farm-to-table Cambodian tasting menu restaurant in Siem Reap (~$35–45 per person, book ahead).

day_by_day.notes: Wear light, breathable clothing and a hat. Bring sunscreen, water, and insect repellent. Modest dress required at temples — shoulders and knees must be covered. November weather is typically dry and pleasant (~25–30°C).

day_by_day.morning: Explore the outer temples of the Angkor complex: Preah Khan (a sprawling jungle monastery), Neak Pean (a beautiful island temple on an artificial lake), and Ta Som (a smaller, intimate temple with dramatic tree roots). Rent bicycles (~$3–5/day) for an eco-friendly and authentic experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Angkor National Museum in Siem Reap town (~$12 entry). This world-class museum provides deep context on Khmer civilization, the Angkor Empire, and Buddhist heritage with stunning artifact displays. Follow with a walk through the Old Market (Psar Chas) to browse spices, silks, and local goods.
day_by_day.evening: Attend an Apsara dance performance — a UNESCO-recognized classical Khmer dance tradition. 'Smile of Angkor' or 'Apsara Theatre' offer dinner-and-show packages (~$25–35).

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at hotel or 'Joma Bakery Café' — fresh pastries, eggs, and good coffee (~$5–8).
meals.lunch: Street food lunch near the Old Market — try bai sach chrouk (pork and rice), nom banh chok (Khmer noodles), or fresh spring rolls (~$2–4).
meals.dinner: Dinner included in the Apsara show package, or dine at 'Malis Restaurant' for refined Cambodian cuisine (~$15–25).

day_by_day.notes: The bicycle route through Angkor's outer temples is flat and scenic — ideal in November's cooler dry season. Start early (by 07:00) to beat the heat and crowds at popular temples.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Beng Mealea — a remote, largely unrestored jungle temple (~40 km from Siem Reap, ~1.5 hours by tuk-tuk). This atmospheric ruin feels like a true archaeological discovery with massive stone blocks draped in jungle vegetation. Far fewer tourists than Angkor.
day_by_day.afternoon: On the return journey, stop at Rolous Group — some of the oldest temples in the Angkor region (9th century), including Preah Ko, Bakong (a massive pyramid temple), and Lolei. These pre-Angkor temples offer fascinating historical contrast.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening in Siem Reap. Visit the vibrant Kandal Village neighborhood for boutique shopping, art galleries, and independent cafés. Enjoy a traditional Khmer massage to recover from the day's walking (~$12–18/hour).

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at hotel before departure.
meals.lunch: Pack a lunch from a local market or eat at a small local restaurant near Beng Mealea village (~$3–6) — a great opportunity to try home-style Cambodian cooking.
meals.dinner: Dinner at 'Haven Restaurant' in Siem Reap — a social enterprise training disadvantaged youth, with excellent Khmer and Western food (~$10–15).

day_by_day.notes: Hire a tuk-tuk for the full day (~$25–35) for Beng Mealea and Rolous. The road to Beng Mealea is now paved and comfortable. Entry to Beng Mealea is ~$5 (separate from Angkor Pass). Bring extra water and snacks.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Take a morning bus or private van transfer from Siem Reap to Phnom Penh (~6 hours, $10–15 by bus or $50–70 private). Book with Mekong Express or Giant Ibis for comfort and reliability. Enjoy the Cambodian countryside scenery en route.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Phnom Penh. Check into a mid-range hotel near the riverside (e.g., Pavilion Hotel or Rambutan Resort, ~$60–90/night). Take a gentle orientation walk along the Sisowath Quay riverfront promenade beside the confluence of the Mekong and Tonlé Sap rivers.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda at golden hour (closes 17:00 — check timing) or admire the illuminated exterior. Stroll the riverside for street food and sunset views over the Mekong.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at hotel before departure from Siem Reap.
meals.lunch: Lunch stop en route or snacks on the bus.
meals.dinner: Dinner at 'Friends Restaurant' (Mith Samlanh) on the Phnom Penh riverside — a beloved social enterprise with excellent Cambodian tapas and cocktails (~$10–18).

day_by_day.notes: Giant Ibis bus is highly recommended for safety and comfort with Wi-Fi and AC. Book tickets in advance online. Phnom Penh is a bustling capital — be aware of your belongings, especially on the riverside.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum (S-21 Prison) — a profoundly important and sobering memorial to the victims of the Khmer Rouge regime (1975–1979). Allow 2–3 hours with an audio guide or local guide for full understanding. A deeply moving and essential experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Choeung Ek Genocidal Center (Killing Fields) ~15 km from the city center — the memorial stupa and peaceful grounds provide important historical closure. Then visit the National Museum of Cambodia near the Royal Palace for Khmer art and sculpture spanning centuries.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Royal Palace complex and Silver Pagoda if not visited yesterday (~$10 entry). The Silver Pagoda houses the famous Emerald Buddha and a life-size gold Buddha encrusted with diamonds. Stroll the Central Market (Phsar Thmei) in the evening.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at hotel or 'Café Central' near the riverside (~$5–8).
meals.lunch: Lunch at 'Romdeng Restaurant' — another acclaimed social enterprise serving traditional Cambodian cuisine including regional specialties (~$10–15).
meals.dinner: Dinner at a riverside restaurant — try 'Topaz' for a refined Cambodian-French fusion experience (~$20–30), or keep it casual at a local riverside eatery (~$8–12).

day_by_day.notes: The Tuol Sleng and Choeung Ek visits are emotionally heavy — allow time for reflection. It is respectful to dress modestly and maintain quiet decorum. Hiring a tuk-tuk for the full day in Phnom Penh is efficient (~$15–20/day).

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Take a morning bus or shared taxi from Phnom Penh to Sihanoukville (~4 hours, $8–12 by bus), then connect by ferry to Koh Rong Samloem island (~45 minutes, ~$25 round trip). This stunning island is one of Cambodia's most beautiful — far less developed than Koh Rong.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Koh Rong Samloem. Check into a mid-range beachfront bungalow at Saracen Bay (e.g., Lazy Beach or M'Pai Bay guesthouses, ~$40–70/night). Spend the afternoon swimming in the crystal-clear turquoise water, relaxing on the white sand beach, and snorkeling the coral reefs.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the spectacular sunset over the Gulf of Thailand from the beach. After dark, look for bioluminescent plankton glowing in the waves — a magical natural phenomenon best seen in calm, dark conditions.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at hotel before departure from Phnom Penh.
meals.lunch: Snack on the ferry or grab food at the Sihanoukville port before boarding.
meals.dinner: Fresh seafood dinner at your beachfront bungalow restaurant or a nearby beach shack — grilled fish, prawns, and squid with rice (~$10–15).

day_by_day.notes: Book ferry tickets in advance, especially on weekends. Bring cash to the island as ATMs are limited or unavailable. Pack light for the island — leave large luggage in a storage facility in Sihanoukville if needed. Sunscreen is essential.

day_by_day.morning: Full beach and island day. Morning snorkeling excursion around the island's coral reefs — book through your guesthouse (~$15–20 including equipment). The reefs around Koh Rong Samloem are home to colorful fish, sea turtles, and vibrant coral.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the island on foot — hike the jungle trail from Saracen Bay to M'Pai Bay village (~45 minutes through lush rainforest) for a glimpse of local island life. Swim at the quieter M'Pai Bay beach. Return by longtail boat (~$3–5).
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the beach. Night swimming to witness the bioluminescent plankton glowing blue in the water — an unforgettable experience. Stargazing on the beach away from light pollution.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at guesthouse — fresh fruit, eggs, and coffee overlooking the beach (~$4–7).
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch at a local shack — try Khmer fried rice, fish amok, or fresh coconut (~$5–8).
meals.dinner: Barbecue seafood dinner on the beach — many guesthouses offer fresh catch of the day grilled over charcoal (~$12–18).

day_by_day.notes: November is an excellent time to visit Cambodia's islands — the dry season brings calm seas, clear water, and good visibility for snorkeling. Respect the fragile coral ecosystem — do not touch or stand on coral. Use reef-safe sunscreen.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning on Koh Rong Samloem — enjoy a peaceful sunrise walk along the beach. Take a kayak out on the calm morning waters (rental ~$5–8/hour). Pack up and take the morning ferry back to Sihanoukville.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Phnom Penh by bus or private transfer (~4 hours). Alternatively, if time allows, spend the afternoon in Sihanoukville exploring Otres Beach — a quieter, more relaxed beach option compared to the main town. Then travel to Phnom Penh for a final night.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Phnom Penh. Visit the lively Bassac Lane bar street for craft cocktails and a vibrant atmosphere. Browse the Night Market along the riverside for last-minute souvenirs — Cambodian silk scarves, kramas (traditional scarves), silver jewelry, and wood carvings.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at island guesthouse before ferry departure.
meals.lunch: Lunch in Sihanoukville before the bus — try a local noodle soup restaurant near the port (~$3–5).
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at 'Khéma Restaurant' in Phnom Penh — a stylish French-Cambodian brasserie with excellent food and ambiance (~$20–30).

day_by_day.notes: Confirm bus and ferry times the day before to ensure smooth connections. Keep a small overnight bag accessible for the final night in Phnom Penh rather than unpacking everything.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Cambodia. If time before departure, visit Wat Phnom — the hilltop temple that gives Phnom Penh its name, a peaceful and historically significant Buddhist shrine in the heart of the city. Light incense and make a small offering for good luck.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on flight time, enjoy a final Cambodian lunch, complete any last-minute shopping at the Central Market (Phsar Thmei) for gems, silks, and handicrafts, and transfer to Phnom Penh International Airport. Allow 2.5–3 hours before departure.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Phnom Penh International Airport. Reflect on 10 incredible days of ancient temples, rich Khmer culture, moving history, and stunning island beaches.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at hotel — enjoy a full Cambodian breakfast with bai sach chrouk (pork and rice porridge) or French-influenced baguettes with pâté, a colonial legacy (~$4–7).
meals.lunch: Final Cambodian meal at 'Sugar Palm Restaurant' — a beloved local institution for authentic Khmer cooking (~$10–15).
meals.dinner: Light meal or snacks at the airport.

day_by_day.notes: Keep a photocopy of your passport and travel documents. Ensure you have no prohibited items (e.g., Buddha images over a certain size may require export permits). Cambodia departure tax is typically included in airline tickets. Exchange remaining Cambodian Riel back to USD before departing — USD is universally accepted and easy to use.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Cambodia Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Angkor Archaeological Park, Siem Reap Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Siem Reap International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged to your boutique stay within the Angkor Archaeological Park area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check-in and settle into your boutique property. Enjoy a welcome drink and orientation with your personal concierge. Take a leisurely stroll through the hotel gardens to acclimatize. Optional: a brief orientation drive around the outer perimeter of Angkor Thom to get your first glimpse of the ancient kingdom.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on your hotel terrace or rooftop overlooking the jungle canopy. Private welcome dinner at the hotel's signature restaurant featuring refined Khmer cuisine — amok trey (fish amok), lok lak beef, and fresh tropical fruit desserts.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (arrival day)
meals.lunch: Light refreshments and welcome snacks upon check-in at the hotel
meals.dinner: Private in-hotel dining — curated Khmer tasting menu with paired Cambodian craft cocktails and imported wines

day_by_day.notes: Arrange a private airport transfer in advance. November is the beginning of the dry season in Cambodia — expect warm, pleasant weather around 28–32°C with minimal rain. Stay hydrated after your flight. Confirm your personal guide for the following days with the concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn private guided tour of Angkor Wat for the iconic sunrise. Arrive by 5:15 AM to secure a prime reflection pool position. Your expert guide will narrate the history of the Khmer Empire as the sun rises over the five towers. Explore the outer gallery bas-reliefs depicting the Churning of the Ocean of Milk and the Battle of Kurukshetra.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the enigmatic Bayon Temple at Angkor Thom — marvel at 216 serene stone faces carved into 54 towers. Continue to the Elephant Terrace and the Terrace of the Leper King. Return to the hotel for a midday rest and a dip in the pool during the hottest hours.
day_by_day.evening: Private sunset visit to Phnom Bakheng hilltop temple (pre-booked permit required — limited access). Panoramic views over the jungle and Angkor Wat silhouette at dusk. Dinner at a top-rated Siem Reap fine dining restaurant such as Cuisine Wat Damnak or Malis Restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Early pre-dawn light breakfast box prepared by the hotel (coffee, pastries, fruit) before the sunrise tour
meals.lunch: Leisurely poolside lunch at the hotel — fresh spring rolls, grilled prawns, tropical salads
meals.dinner: Fine dining at Cuisine Wat Damnak — contemporary Cambodian tasting menu using locally sourced ingredients, wine pairing available

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book the Phnom Bakheng sunset permit well in advance as it is strictly limited. Wear comfortable walking shoes and light breathable clothing. Bring a light layer for the early morning. Angkor Archaeological Park pass (3-day or 7-day) should be purchased upon arrival or pre-arranged by your concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided exploration of Ta Prohm — the atmospheric 'Tomb Raider' temple dramatically engulfed by massive strangler fig and silk-cotton trees. Visit early to beat the crowds. Continue to Preah Khan, a sprawling monastic complex with long colonnaded corridors, hidden courtyards, and intricate carvings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Exclusive Angkor Wat interior deep-dive — revisit the temple with a specialist art historian guide to explore the upper levels (pre-booked access), inner sanctum, and intricate devata carvings in detail. Followed by a private tuk-tuk ride through the ancient city walls of Angkor Thom.
day_by_day.evening: Traditional Apsara dance performance at a premium venue (e.g., Temple Club or a private performance arranged at your hotel). Dinner featuring royal Khmer cuisine inspired by ancient palace recipes.

meals.breakfast: Full à la carte breakfast at the hotel — eggs Benedict, fresh tropical juices, Cambodian rice porridge (bobor), artisan coffee
meals.lunch: Elegant picnic lunch arranged by the hotel amid the temple grounds — charcuterie, sandwiches, fresh fruits, chilled beverages
meals.dinner: Royal Khmer dinner at a heritage restaurant with live Apsara performance — amok, beef loc lak, Khmer red curry, sticky rice with mango

day_by_day.notes: The Angkor Wat upper levels require advance booking and have a strict visitor cap. Wear modest clothing covering shoulders and knees for temple entry. A private Apsara performance can be arranged at select luxury hotels for an intimate cultural experience.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the remote and rarely visited Beng Mealea temple — a vast 12th-century jungle-swallowed ruin located about 68 km east of Siem Reap. Travel in a private air-conditioned vehicle. The temple is largely unrestored, offering a raw and adventurous archaeological experience with your expert guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: En route back, stop at Banteay Srei — the 'Citadel of Women' — renowned for its extraordinarily intricate pink sandstone carvings considered the finest in all of Angkor. Visit Banteay Samré nearby for a quieter, equally impressive experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siem Reap. Relax with a traditional Khmer herbal massage and spa treatment at your hotel's luxury spa. Private dinner on your hotel terrace under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Full hotel breakfast before the early departure
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic lunch in the jungle setting near Beng Mealea — prepared by your hotel with chilled drinks and premium local snacks
meals.dinner: Private terrace dinner at the hotel — grilled lobster, Cambodian herb salads, premium wine selection

day_by_day.notes: Beng Mealea requires a separate entry ticket. Roads are good but the journey takes approximately 1.5 hours each way — depart early (7:00 AM) to make the most of the day. Wear sturdy footwear as the temple involves climbing over rubble and uneven surfaces. Insect repellent is strongly recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise boat tour on Tonlé Sap Lake — one of Southeast Asia's most remarkable freshwater ecosystems and a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve. Cruise through floating villages (Chong Kneas or Kampong Phluk) on a private boat. Witness the unique lifestyle of communities living entirely on water, with floating schools, temples, and markets.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Artisans Angkor workshop and fair-trade boutique in Siem Reap — observe master craftspeople recreating ancient Khmer silk weaving, lacquerware, and stone carving techniques. Opportunity for curated luxury souvenir shopping. Followed by a visit to the Angkor National Museum for a world-class overview of Khmer civilization and artifacts.
day_by_day.evening: Siem Reap evening exploration — a private guided walk through the vibrant Pub Street area and Old French Quarter. Dinner at one of Siem Reap's most acclaimed restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the hotel before the boat departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at a recommended riverside restaurant in Siem Reap — fresh Tonlé Sap fish dishes, Khmer noodle soup (kuy teav), tropical fruit
meals.dinner: Dinner at Malis Restaurant — sophisticated modern Cambodian cuisine in an elegant open-air garden setting

day_by_day.notes: November water levels on Tonlé Sap are high (post-rainy season), making it an ideal time to visit the floating villages. Kampong Phluk offers a more authentic and less touristy experience than Chong Kneas. Book the private boat in advance through your concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Private transfer to Siem Reap Airport for a short domestic flight to Phnom Penh (approximately 45 minutes). Check into a luxury hotel in Phnom Penh (e.g., Rosewood Phnom Penh or Raffles Hotel Le Royal). Brief orientation walk along the Tonlé Sap and Mekong riverfront promenade.
day_by_day.afternoon: Guided visit to the Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda — the stunning official residence of the King of Cambodia, featuring gilded spires, Khmer and French colonial architecture, and the celebrated Emerald Buddha. Continue to the National Museum of Cambodia, home to the world's finest collection of Khmer sculpture and artifacts.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a rooftop bar overlooking the confluence of the Mekong and Tonlé Sap rivers. Dinner at a premier Phnom Penh restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast in Siem Reap before departure
meals.lunch: Riverside lunch in Phnom Penh — fresh seafood, Khmer salads, coconut-based curries at a refined riverfront restaurant
meals.dinner: Dinner at Topaz Restaurant or Mea Culpa — French-Cambodian fine dining with an extensive wine cellar

day_by_day.notes: Book the domestic flight in advance (Cambodia Angkor Air or similar). The Royal Palace has a strict dress code — shoulders and knees must be covered. Photography restrictions apply inside the Silver Pagoda. Phnom Penh is a larger city — use your hotel's private car service for transfers.

day_by_day.morning: Sobering but essential visit to the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum (S-21 Prison) — a former high school turned Khmer Rouge detention center, now a powerful memorial and museum. Continue to the Choeung Ek Genocidal Center (Killing Fields) — a UNESCO-recognized memorial site with an atmospheric audio guide and Buddhist stupa containing victims' remains. A deeply moving and historically significant experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Recovery and cultural contrast: explore the French colonial architecture of Phnom Penh's riverside district. Visit the Central Market (Phsar Thmei) — a stunning Art Deco landmark with four wings selling jewelry, silks, antiques, and local crafts. Afternoon spa treatment at your luxury hotel.
day_by_day.evening: Private sunset cruise on the Mekong River aboard a chartered boat with champagne and canapés. Dinner at a top Phnom Penh establishment.

meals.breakfast: Full à la carte breakfast at the hotel
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a café near the Central Market — Cambodian sandwiches (num pang), fresh juices, local desserts
meals.dinner: Dinner at Khéma Restaurant or The Plantation — sophisticated Cambodian and French cuisine in a refined colonial setting

day_by_day.notes: The Tuol Sleng and Choeung Ek visits are emotionally heavy — allow time for reflection. Hiring a knowledgeable guide for these sites is strongly recommended to provide proper historical context. The Mekong sunset cruise should be booked through your hotel concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Private transfer from Phnom Penh to Kep or Kampot (approximately 2.5–3 hours by private car) — Cambodia's charming coastal and riverside provinces. Check into a luxury boutique property (e.g., Knai Bang Chatt in Kep or The Columns in Kampot). Morning walk along Kep's seaside promenade with views over the Gulf of Thailand.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the famous Kep Crab Market — try freshly caught blue crabs cooked with Kampot pepper, one of the world's most prized spices. Explore Kep National Park — a forested hill with jungle trails, butterfly valley, and panoramic coastal views. Alternatively, take a private boat to Rabbit Island (Koh Tonsay) for a tranquil afternoon on a pristine beach.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset from the clifftop terrace of your hotel or a scenic viewpoint. Dinner featuring Kampot pepper crab and fresh seafood — the definitive local culinary experience.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the Phnom Penh hotel before departure
meals.lunch: Kep Crab Market — fresh blue crab with Kampot pepper, grilled seafood, cold Angkor beer in a casual open-air setting
meals.dinner: Fine dining at Knai Bang Chatt's Sailing Club Restaurant — seafood tasting menu with Kampot pepper specialties and coastal views

day_by_day.notes: November is an excellent time to visit the coast — dry season has begun with warm, sunny weather. Kampot pepper is a premium local product — purchase some at the source as a luxury souvenir. Book Rabbit Island boat transfers through your hotel. The drive from Phnom Penh is scenic — request a stop at Takeo province's ancient temples if interested.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided kayaking or stand-up paddleboarding along the Kampot River through mangrove forests and past colonial-era buildings. Visit a Kampot pepper farm for an exclusive behind-the-scenes tour — learn about cultivation, harvesting, and grading of this world-renowned spice. Tasting session included.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Kampot town — a beautifully preserved French colonial riverside town with pastel-colored architecture, art galleries, and boutique shops. Visit the old Kampot durian market (seasonal). Alternatively, arrange a private boat trip along the Praek Tuek Chhu River to spot wildlife including kingfishers, monitor lizards, and river otters.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner cocktails on a floating bar on the Kampot River. Farewell dinner in Kampot at a top riverside restaurant — fresh river fish, Kampot pepper steak, local rice wine.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at your boutique hotel — fresh tropical fruits, eggs, Cambodian rice dishes, artisan coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at a recommended Kampot riverside restaurant — Khmer fish curry, fresh spring rolls, coconut soup
meals.dinner: Dinner at Rikitikitavi or The Rusty Keyhole — acclaimed riverside dining with an extensive menu of Cambodian and international cuisine

day_by_day.notes: Kampot pepper farm visits should be pre-arranged. Several premium farms offer exclusive private tours. The Kampot River is calm and ideal for kayaking in November. Purchase authentic Kampot pepper (red, black, white, and green varieties) directly from certified farms for the highest quality product.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely final morning — sleep in, enjoy a long breakfast, and take a last stroll along the Kampot riverside or relax by the hotel pool. Optional: a final spa treatment or yoga session at the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private transfer back to Phnom Penh International Airport (approximately 2.5–3 hours). En route, optional stop at Phnom Chisor — an 11th-century hilltop temple with sweeping views over the surrounding plains, offering a final taste of Cambodia's ancient heritage. Airport check-in and departure formalities.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Phnom Penh International Airport. Farewell to Cambodia.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent final breakfast at the boutique hotel — full spread with local and international options, fresh juices, specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the hotel or a packed gourmet lunch box for the road journey
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or an early dinner at a Phnom Penh airport-area restaurant before departure

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before your international flight for check-in and immigration at Phnom Penh International Airport. Confirm your private transfer the evening before. Duty-free shopping at the airport offers Cambodian silk, Kampot pepper, and locally made jewelry. Ensure all temple passes, receipts, and travel documents are organized. A 10% tip for your personal guide is customary and greatly appreciated.
